questions.question: Newton's law of universal gravitation states that the force of attraction between two point masses is directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the
options: Square of the distance between them
Cube of the distance between them
questions.explanation: Newton's law: F ∝ m1m2 / r2. The force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance between the masses.

questions.question: The gravitational force between two masses of 2kg and 8kg separated by a distance of 2m is [G = 6.67 × 10<sup>-11</sup>Nm<sup>2</sup>kg<sup>-2</sup>]
The S.I. unit of the gravitational constant G is
questions.explanation: From F = G m<sub>1</sub>m<sub>2</sub> / r<sup>2</sup>, we get G = F r<sup>2</sup> / (m<sub>1</sub>m<sub>2</sub>). Units: N m<sup>2</sup> kg<sup>-2</sup>.

questions.question: If the distance between two masses is doubled, the gravitational force between them becomes
questions.explanation: F ∝ 1/r2. If r → 2r, then F' = F / (2)2 = F/4, i.e., one-quarter.

questions.question: If the distance between two masses is halved, the gravitational force between them becomes
questions.explanation: F ∝ 1/r2. If r → r/2, then F' = F / (1/2)2 = 4F, i.e., four times.

questions.question: Gravitational field intensity at a point is defined as the gravitational force per unit
questions.explanation: Gravitational field intensity g = F/m, which is the force per unit mass.

questions.question: The S.I. unit of gravitational field intensity is
questions.explanation: g = F/m, so unit = N/kg = N kg-1.

questions.question: The gravitational field intensity at a distance r from a mass M is given by
questions.explanation: The gravitational field intensity due to a point mass M is g = GM/r2.

questions.question: The gravitational field intensity at the surface of the earth is equal to
options: The acceleration due to gravity g
questions.explanation: At the earth's surface, the gravitational field intensity is exactly the acceleration due to gravity g.

questions.question: The acceleration due to gravity g at the surface of the earth is given by
questions.explanation: g = GM/R<sup>2</sup>, where M is the mass of the earth and R is its radius.

questions.question: The value of acceleration due to gravity g at the surface of the earth is approximately
questions.explanation: The standard value of g at the earth's surface is approximately 9.8 m/s2.

questions.question: As the altitude above the earth's surface increases, the value of g
questions.explanation: g is inversely proportional to the square of the distance from the centre. As altitude increases, distance increases, so g decreases.

questions.question: The value of g at a height h above the earth's surface is given by
questions.explanation: At height h, g<sub>h</sub> = GM/(R+h)<sup>2</sup> = g (R/(R+h))<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: The value of g at a depth d below the earth's surface is given by
questions.explanation: At depth d, g<sub>d</sub> = g(1 - d/R), where R is the earth's radius.

questions.question: At the centre of the earth, the value of g is
options: Equal to g at the surface
questions.explanation: At the centre of the earth, the mass enclosed is zero, so g = 0.

questions.question: The value of g at the equator is slightly less than that at the poles because of
options: The shape of the earth and its rotation
The magnetic field of the earth
questions.explanation: The earth is oblate (flattened at poles) and rotates. The centripetal effect reduces g at the equator.

questions.question: The weight of a body is
options: The force of gravity on the body
questions.explanation: Weight is the force of gravity acting on a body: W = mg.

questions.question: A body of mass 10kg has a weight on the earth's surface of approximately
The mass of a body is
questions.explanation: Mass is a scalar quantity and is constant everywhere.

questions.question: The weight of a body on the moon compared to that on earth is
questions.explanation: The moon's gravitational field is weaker (g ≈ 1.6 m/s2), so weight is less.

questions.question: The gravitational potential at a distance r from a point mass M is given by
questions.explanation: Gravitational potential is V = -GM/r. The negative sign indicates it is attractive.

questions.question: The S.I. unit of gravitational potential is
questions.explanation: Potential = work done per unit mass, so unit = J/kg = J kg-1.

questions.question: The gravitational potential at infinity is taken as
questions.explanation: By convention, gravitational potential at infinity is zero.

questions.question: Gravitational potential energy of a mass m at a distance r from a mass M is given by
questions.explanation: Gravitational potential energy is U = -GMm/r.

questions.question: The escape velocity from the earth's surface is given by
questions.explanation: Escape velocity is vesc = √(2GM/R).

questions.question: The escape velocity from the earth's surface is approximately
questions.explanation: The escape velocity from Earth is approximately 11.2 km/s.

questions.question: The escape velocity of a body from the earth's surface depends on the
options: Mass of the earth and radius of the earth
questions.explanation: vesc = √(2GM/R), so it depends on the mass and radius of the earth, not on the mass of the body.

questions.question: The escape velocity of a body from the earth's surface is independent of the
questions.explanation: vesc = √(2GM/R), so it is independent of the mass of the body.

questions.question: A satellite is in a circular orbit around the earth. The gravitational force provides the
questions.explanation: The gravitational force acts as the centripetal force that keeps the satellite in orbit.

questions.question: The orbital speed of a satellite in a circular orbit of radius r around the earth is given by
questions.explanation: Orbital speed is v = √(GM/r).

questions.question: The period of a satellite in a circular orbit of radius r around the earth is given by
questions.explanation: Period of a satellite is T = 2π√(r3/GM).

questions.question: Kepler's third law states that the square of the period of revolution of a planet is directly proportional to the
options: Cube of the radius of its orbit
Square of the radius of its orbit
Inverse of the radius of its orbit
questions.explanation: Kepler's third law: T2 ∝ r3, i.e., directly proportional to the cube of the radius.

questions.question: Kepler's first law states that the orbit of a planet around the sun is
options: An ellipse with the sun at one focus
questions.explanation: Kepler's first law: the orbit is an ellipse with the sun at one focus.

questions.question: Kepler's second law (law of areas) states that the line joining the planet to the sun sweeps out equal areas in equal
questions.explanation: Kepler's second law: equal areas are swept out in equal times.

questions.question: A satellite in a parking orbit has a period
options: Less than the earth's period of rotation
More than the earth's period of rotation
Equal to the earth's period of rotation
questions.explanation: A parking orbit is a geostationary orbit, so its period is equal to the earth's period of rotation (24 hours).

questions.question: A geostationary satellite has a period of approximately
questions.explanation: A geostationary satellite has a period of 24 hours.

questions.question: A geostationary satellite must be located
questions.explanation: A geostationary satellite must be located above the equator to remain stationary relative to the earth.

questions.question: The weight of a body at the centre of the earth is
questions.explanation: At the centre, g = 0, so weight = mg = zero.

questions.question: The gravitational field intensity inside a hollow spherical shell is
questions.explanation: Inside a hollow spherical shell, the gravitational field intensity is zero.

questions.question: The gravitational potential inside a hollow spherical shell is
options: Constant and equal to that on the surface
questions.explanation: The gravitational potential inside a hollow shell is constant and equal to its value on the surface.

questions.question: The gravitational force between two bodies is called a
questions.explanation: Gravitational force is a field force (action at a distance).

questions.question: The gravitational constant G has a value of approximately
questions.explanation: The gravitational constant G ≈ 6.67 × 10-11 N m2 kg-2.

questions.question: The gravitational force between two bodies is the weakest when
options: The distance between them is small
The distance between them is large
questions.explanation: F ∝ 1/r2, so the force is weakest when the distance is large.

questions.question: Two bodies of masses m<sub>1</sub> and m<sub>2</sub> are separated by a distance r. If the mass of one body is doubled and the distance is also doubled, the new gravitational force is
questions.explanation: F = G m1m2 / r2. New: m1' = 2m1, r' = 2r. F' = G(2m1)m2/(2r)2 = 2Gm1m2/(4r2) = F/2. So half.

questions.question: The gravitational potential energy of a body at the earth's surface is
questions.explanation: U = -GMm/R, which is negative.

questions.question: The total mechanical energy of a satellite in a stable circular orbit is
questions.explanation: Total energy E = -GMm/(2r), which is negative.

questions.question: The period of a simple pendulum on the moon compared to that on the earth is
questions.explanation: T = 2π√(L/g). Since g is smaller on the moon, T is longer.

questions.question: The value of g on the moon is approximately
questions.explanation: The acceleration due to gravity on the moon is about 1.6 m/s2.

questions.question: If the radius of the earth is R and the acceleration due to gravity at its surface is g, the escape velocity is given by
questions.explanation: Escape velocity v<sub>esc</sub> = √(2GM/R) = √(2gR), since g = GM/R<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: A satellite moves in a circular orbit of radius 4R around the earth, where R is the radius of the earth. If g is the acceleration due to gravity at the earth's surface, the acceleration of the satellite is
questions.explanation: a = GM/(4R)<sup>2</sup> = GM/(16R<sup>2</sup>) = g/16.
